summary: Staggered webhook fanout causing premature queue-rejects and throttled callbacks
description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightCart Labs reports that a nightly webhook fanout (staggered by tenant workers) is triggering early queue rejections that look like 429 throttles from our edge. Behavior started after they increased parallel webhook workers from 6 -> 18 on their dedicated pool.

Impact:
- ~18% of webhook callbacks are responded to with 429s or dropped before being dispatched to downstream customer endpoints during the job window (03:00-04:30 UTC).
- Median callback latency for successful deliveries increased from 120ms -> 420ms during the spike.
- Customer reports downstream retry storms and duplicate events.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool (BrightCart Labs reserved capacity) in us-east.
- Webhook dispatcher v2.3.1 (deployed 2026-02-28).
- Rate-limiter sidecar uses token-window refill 1s and burst credit of 5 per API-key.

Observed behavior vs expected:
- Expected: fanout workers should remain under tenant token windows; excess requests should be queued and retried with exponential backoff.
- Observed: edge returns 429s quickly and dispatcher marks several queued jobs as REJECTED with "early-queue-reject" reason. Token headers in responses show partial refill but total tenant token count dropped to zero faster than traffic would suggest.

Business impact: enterprise customer experiencing duplicated downstream work and SLA degradation for webhook delivery.
steps_to_reproduce: On a dedicated tenant in us-east, configure webhook worker pool size to 18 with staggered start (interval 200ms).
Trigger a bulk webhook fanout of 12k callbacks across 15 minutes (simulate nightly batch).
Observe dispatcher logs and edge responses; watch for 429s and REJECTED queue states in dispatcher metrics.
Compare token headers on the 429 responses with account-level quota from the console.
Reduce worker pool to 6 and repeat; note behavior returns to expected (no early rejections).
logs: 2026-03-10T03:05:12Z dispatcher INFO callback queued tenant=brightcart job_id=fc-99321 delay=0ms
2026-03-10T03:05:13Z edge WARN 429 tenant=brightcart route=/webhook callback_id=cb-4421 X-RateLimit-Remaining=0 X-RateLimit-Reset=1s
2026-03-10T03:05:13Z dispatcher ERROR early-queue-reject tenant=brightcart job_id=fc-99324 reason=token-window-exhausted metrics_ref=grafana:gw.rate.windows
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: rate-limiter token-window misconfiguration with burst credits insufficient for synchronized fanout.

Found: token accounting is per-API-key but dispatcher uses signed temporary worker tokens; TTL rotation created short-lived parallel token windows that double-counted when multiple workers refreshed in lockstep.
Edge behavior: when token bucket hits zero, edge emits 429 quickly; dispatcher marks queued jobs as REJECTED after a small soft-queue timeout (configured low to avoid stale dispatches).
Rate-limiter config: refill_interval=1s, burst_tokens=5, tenant_capacity=1200 tokens/s. With 18 workers and 200ms stagger, observed microbursts consumed available burst credits faster than expected.
Evidence: correlation between signed-url rotation events (timestamped 03:04:59Z) and the first major drop in X-RateLimit-Remaining across worker traces.
comments: Maya Chen (2026-03-10T10:32Z): Customer opened saying this started after they increased worker count. Provided example request IDs and traces.

Rafael Ortiz (2026-03-10T12:05Z): Reproduced in staging with dedicated replica. Observed early-queue-reject when we align rotation window with worker starts. Adding SRE for rate-limiter review. #support @sre-team

Priya Nair (SRE) (2026-03-10T13:10Z): Looking at rate-limiter code path; suspect signed-token refresh creates new token buckets for short-lived credentials causing temporary parallel accounting. Running a debug build to log token-bucket allocation per token-id.
BrightCart (customer) (2026-03-10T14:45Z): We can throttle worker ramp to 100ms->500ms as a stopgap. Need guidance for permanent fix; concerned about nightly window SLA.

Rafael Ortiz (2026-03-11T09:21Z): Temporary mitigation: recommend increasing dispatcher soft-queue timeout from 250ms->2s and set worker staggering to 500ms. Also propose adjusting tenant burst_tokens to 10 for the dedicated pool while we patch accounting.
resolution: Workaround applied: BrightCart increased stagger interval and dispatcher queue timeout; tenant burst_tokens temporarily raised. Engineering patch in progress to dedupe token-bucket creation on short-lived signed tokens (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/7203). Follow-up: change will centralize token accounting at tenant level to avoid per-signed-token buckets. Target rollout to prod us-east 2026-03-15.
